title: Chelsea fan group announces protest plans for FA Cup final and during Tottenham game
content:
A Chelsea supporters group has confirmed plans to stage a protest against the club’s ownership and board in two of their upcoming fixtures.

NotAProjectCFC confirmed that the their show of “no faith” will take place before the FA Cup final against Manchester City on May 16 and against London rivals Tottenham Hotspur on May 19.

Chelsea’s 3-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest on Monday means they have suffered six Premier League defeats in a row, their worst run since 1993, and are ninth in the table, 10 points off Aston Villa in fifth place.

Liam Rosenior replaced Enzo Maresca as head coach in January, signing a six-year deal, but was sacked in April after only 107 days at the club. Calum McFarlane has been placed in interim charge of the side until the end of the season.

In recent months, supporters have also grown increasingly frustrated with the club’s ownership group BlueCo — a consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital — their multi-club model that also sees them control French team Strasbourg and the team’s transfer policy.

NotAProjectCFC said that it had planned a protest march on Wembley Way before the final against City at Wembley Stadium and would involve a banner directed not only at BlueCo but the club’s sporting directors, Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart.

Against Tottenham, the planned protest involves fans at Stamford Bridge turning their back to the pitch in the 22nd minute (in reference to the year BlueCo purchased the team in for one minute and chanting “we want our Chelsea back”.

“While we recognise the importance of both matches, we feel these steps are absolutely necessary in an attempt to send a public message that we have no faith in the current ownership and the direction the club is heading,” NotAProjectCFC said in a statement on Monday.

“Given the unprecedented expenditure on the men’s first team since Blueco acquired the club, this is absolutely unacceptable.

“The issues at the club go far beyond any manager. Until meaningful change is brought about to the environment in which they operate, the identity of these managers will be futile. We also have no faith that the club is entering any period of ‘self-reflection’ as stated. We are interested in actions, not words.

“Claiming you are taking a period of self-reflection is meaningless if those in control do not publicly outline the mistakes they have identified nor outline how they plan to rectify them.

“These protest actions will continue beyond the end of this season, and will not cease until we have forced change.”

Before the 1-0 defeat against Manchester United on April 18, NotAProjectCFC staged a protest against BlueCo outside Stamford Bridge, alongside Strasbourg fans.

Two days before the protest, Clearlake co-founder Behdad Eghbali addressed the fans’ concerns.

“For the fans, we care,” he said when asked about his message for Chelsea supporters. “We want the club to be successful. We’re focused on delivering that on-pitch performance. I think six months ago everyone was super-happy. Results have been mixed, disappointing more recently. There’s a full reflection on what we can do better, what we can improve on.

“There is a plan. We reflect on the plan. We try to improve the plan and tweak the plan if it’s not working. The message is we’re committed.”

Before Chelsea head to Wembley, they visit Liverpool in Premier League action on Saturday.
